title: Mycobacterium mageritense
extracted_sentences: Mycobacterium mageritense is a species of rapidly growing microorganism in the genus Mycobacterium .
This species causes Lymphadentis in children.
In adults, '''M.
mageritense''' causes pneumonia .
Magerit, is Arabic for Madrid, where it was first isolated from human sputum.
This species is a gram-positive, nonmotile and strongly acid-fast rods.
Their colonies are smooth, mucoid and nonphotochromogenic colonies.
Members of this species have rapid growth on Lowenstein-Jensen medium at 22 degC, 30 degC, 37 degC and 45 degC within 2-4 days.
Their optimum growth at 30 degC and 37 degC.
M. mageritense is resistant to isoniazid, cycloserine, capreomycin, pyrazinamide, and thiosemicarbazone.
Most strains are also resistant to ethambutol.
This species can be characterized by unique hsp65 gene, 16S rDNA and sodA sequences.
They are closely related to ''M.
fortuitum and M.
peregrinum'' at the DNA homology level.
They can also be differentiation from ''M.
fortuitum'' by its growth at 45 degC and by its use of mannitol as a sole carbon source.
It has a Biosafety level 1.
Mycobacterium mageritense was first isolated from a human (Homo spaien) sputum in Madrid.
